topics.display_title: Caste System: Structure and Contemporary Dynamics

panels.title: Level of analysis
ascii_lines: VARNA -> four-fold textual ideal type, normative
JATI -> local endogamous birth group, observable
SUB-JATI -> narrower endogamy circle inside a jati
RULE -> answer at the jati level, argue with the varna template
MUST REMEMBER: Caste joins varna ideology, locally ranked jatis, endogamy, hereditary
occupation, purity-pollution, social closure and power; Sanskritisation, dominant caste,
secularisation, politicisation and caste-class mobility explain change without implying
disappearance.
source_references: Varna, jati and the level problem

panels.title: Four features and their rate of change
ascii_lines: ENDOGAMY -> most consistently observed, changes least
HIERARCHY -> locally ranked by purity and pollution
HEREDITARY MEMBERSHIP -> fixed by birth
OCCUPATION LINK -> weakest joint, broken by urban work

panels.title: Marriage rules that operate together
ascii_lines: CASTE ENDOGAMY -> marry within the jati
GOTRA EXOGAMY -> marry outside the clan lineage
RESULT -> a bounded but non-consanguineous marriage circle
CONSEQUENCE -> caste is reproduced generation by generation

panels.title: Mobility strategies
ascii_lines: SANSKRITISATION -> emulate a locally higher-status caste
EFFECT -> claims rank inside the existing hierarchy
WESTERNISATION -> new values from Western contact
EFFECT -> can subvert the hierarchy rather than confirm it

panels.title: Dominant caste test
ascii_lines: NUMBERS -> is the caste locally numerous
LAND -> does it hold a significant share of local land
OFFICE -> does it control political and Panchayat positions
VERDICT -> dominance can sit below the ritual top

panels.title: Caste and class
ascii_lines: OVERLAP -> caste rank and economic class coincide locally
CROSS-CUTTING -> rich and poor households inside one caste
DRIVER -> urban employment and market credentials
LIMIT -> the overlap is loosening, not abolished
CLOSE DISTINCTION: Varna is not jati, caste is not class, ritual rank is not identical to
economic or political power, untouchability is not every caste inequality, and
constitutional Scheduled Caste status is a legal-administrative category rather than a
complete sociological map.

panels.title: Associational reinvention
ascii_lines: WEAKENED -> occupational allocation and public purity enforcement
REPLACED BY -> caste associations, trusts and electoral blocs
UNCHANGED -> endogamy and intimate-sphere discrimination
VERDICT -> change of register, not disappearance

panels.title: Fluid and static resolved by level
ascii_lines: STATIC LAYER -> endogamy, hereditary membership, segregation
FLUID LAYER -> rank claims, dominance, market mobility
WHY -> rank is locally constructed, boundary is marital
ANSWER -> the paradox is a level distinction, not a contradiction

panels.title: Identity axes by arena
ascii_lines: MARRIAGE -> jati and sub-jati decide the boundary
SHRINE AND DEVOTION -> sect through doctrine and lineage
ELECTORAL MOBILISATION -> jati clusters and religion
DEVELOPMENT GRIEVANCE -> region and language

panels.title: Two marriage boundaries
ascii_lines: INTERCASTE -> parity protects status and resource base
INTERRELIGIOUS -> belonging, kinship and community sanction
CIVIL ROUTE -> Special Marriage Act, 1954 exists across religions
VERDICT -> different guards, therefore different speeds
source_references: Marriage boundaries and the civil route

panels.title: Measurement status
ascii_lines: PIB 30 APRIL 2025 -> caste enumeration announced for Census 2027
GAZETTE S.O. 2681(E) -> fixes the reference dates
STATUS -> prospective, so no caste count may be quoted
LIMIT -> not India's first historical caste enumeration
source_references: Measurement status and the complete answer spine

panels.title: Caste answer spine
ascii_lines: OPEN -> name the level and the demand family
BODY -> structure, mobility, dominance, association
TENSION -> what changed against what did not
CLOSE -> arena-specific verdict with the measurement caveat
EVIDENCE LIMIT: Articles 15-17, 46, 330-342A and reservation institutions set legal
boundaries, but legal prohibition does not equal social eradication; compare Jat, Maratha,
Patidar, Dalit and regional caste dynamics without homogenising communities or inferring
causes from aggregate correlations.
source_references: Measurement status and the complete answer spine
